benchmark.category: an AI system-architect web tool that turns a plain-language description into an Unreal Engine 5 event graph, pseudocode, C++ and setup guide, with cloud projects, file attachments and team sharing
benchmark.users: solo UE5 developers and small game teams — designers, programmers and leads — who describe a gameplay system, tune it, save it to their account and share it or hand out a read-only link

requirements.source_phrase: A shop owner signs up with an email and password and lands in their own new workspace
requirements.statement: A visitor can sign up with an email and password from /signup and lands in a new, empty workspace of their own whose name reads exactly as entered
requirements.notes: Entry point for every other flow; the workspace name is the value the user typed, not a generated default.

requirements.source_phrase: A shop owner signs up with an email and password and lands in their own new workspace
requirements.statement: POST /api/auth/signup stores the user and creates exactly one workspace owned by that user; a second signup with the same email is refused and stores no second user
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of signup: uniqueness of the email is enforced by the store, not only by the form.

requirements.source_phrase: a member signs in with their email and password and sees their workspace
requirements.statement: Signing in at /signin with a seeded account's credentials lands on the dashboard listing that account's own products and nothing from another workspace

requirements.source_phrase: a member signs in with their email and password and sees their workspace
requirements.statement: POST /api/auth/signin returns a session for correct credentials and refuses a wrong password with no session and no token in the response

requirements.source_phrase: The testing system depends on these two accounts and these exact passwords
requirements.statement: The two seeded accounts owner@shop.test / Owner123! and staff@shop.test / Staff123! both sign in, and each belongs to exactly one workspace named in the seed (the owner's workspace and the second workspace respectively)
requirements.notes: Every later phase seeds from these values; the cross-tenant checks depend on the two accounts living in different workspaces.

requirements.source_phrase: Users can add a product with a name, SKU, unit cost, quantity and low-stock threshold
requirements.statement: Submitting the add-product form with a name, SKU, unit cost, quantity and low-stock threshold adds a row to the product list showing exactly the entered values

requirements.source_phrase: Users can add a product with a name, SKU, unit cost, quantity and low-stock threshold
requirements.statement: POST /api/products stores every field the form sends (name, sku, unit_cost, quantity, low_stock_threshold) and GET /api/products/{id} from a new session returns those same values

requirements.source_phrase: The product list shows each product's name, SKU, on-hand quantity and stock value
requirements.statement: /products lists the workspace's products with name, SKU, quantity, unit cost and stock value per row, and the list renders an explicit empty message rather than a blank area when the workspace has no products

requirements.source_phrase: The product list shows each product's name, SKU, on-hand quantity and stock value
requirements.statement: GET /api/products returns every product of the caller's workspace with its stock value computed from the stored quantity and unit cost, and returns an empty list (not an error) for a workspace with no products

requirements.source_phrase: Users can edit a product's name, unit cost and low-stock threshold
requirements.statement: Editing a product's name, unit cost or threshold from its detail screen saves the change, the row updates in place, and a page reload still shows the new values

requirements.source_phrase: Users can edit a product's name, unit cost and low-stock threshold
requirements.statement: PATCH /api/products/{id} persists each edited field and GET /api/products/{id} from a new session returns the new values, leaving unedited fields unchanged

requirements.source_phrase: Users can delete a product they no longer stock
requirements.statement: Deleting a product asks for confirmation naming the product, removes its row from the list, and the row is still gone after a page reload

requirements.source_phrase: Users can delete a product they no longer stock
requirements.statement: DELETE /api/products/{id} removes the product and its stock movements; GET /api/products/{id} afterwards returns not-found and the product no longer appears in any listing or count

requirements.source_phrase: Staff record stock coming in and going out as movements rather than overwriting the number
requirements.statement: Recording a stock movement of +10 or -3 on a product's detail screen changes the on-hand quantity by exactly that delta and adds a line to the movement history showing the delta, the resulting quantity, the author and the time
requirements.notes: The movement is a delta, not an absolute overwrite; the history line is what proves it.

requirements.source_phrase: Staff record stock coming in and going out as movements rather than overwriting the number
requirements.statement: POST /api/products/{id}/movements with a delta stores the movement, moves the stored quantity by that delta, and GET /api/products/{id}/movements from a new session lists it with author and timestamp

requirements.source_phrase: Products below their threshold are flagged low in the list
requirements.statement: A product whose on-hand quantity is at or below its low-stock threshold shows a low-stock badge on the list and detail screens, and the badge disappears once stock is raised above the threshold

requirements.source_phrase: Products below their threshold are flagged low in the list
requirements.statement: GET /api/products?low_stock=true returns exactly the caller's workspace products whose quantity is at or below their own threshold, and excludes a product one unit above its threshold
requirements.notes: Boundary case: quantity equal to the threshold counts as low; one unit above does not.

requirements.source_phrase: The dashboard shows total inventory value and how many products are low on stock
requirements.statement: /dashboard shows the workspace's total inventory value and the count of low-stock products, and both figures change on screen after a stock movement is recorded

requirements.source_phrase: The dashboard shows total inventory value and how many products are low on stock
requirements.statement: GET /api/dashboard returns total inventory value equal to the sum over the workspace's products of quantity times unit cost, rounded to the cent, plus a low-stock count equal to the number of rows the low-stock filter returns
requirements.notes: Inputs: stored quantity and unit_cost per product; formula sum(qty*cost); units are the workspace currency's minor unit; half-up rounding to the cent.

requirements.source_phrase: Users can search products by name or SKU and filter by category
requirements.statement: Typing a word from a product name or SKU into the search box lists the matching products and no product from another workspace, and clearing the box restores the full list

requirements.source_phrase: Users can search products by name or SKU and filter by category
requirements.statement: GET /api/products?q={term} matches on name and SKU case-insensitively and returns only rows from the caller's workspace; the filter offers every category value the stored data holds, not only a hard-coded list

requirements.source_phrase: An owner can invite teammates by email into their workspace
requirements.statement: An owner can invite a teammate by email from the members screen, the invite appears as pending with the address typed, and the invited person signing in with that address joins the same workspace

requirements.source_phrase: An owner can invite teammates by email into their workspace
requirements.statement: POST /api/workspaces/{id}/invites records the invitation bound to that workspace; accepting it adds the user to that workspace only and never to another workspace with the same email domain

requirements.source_phrase: These limits must be enforced on the server, not merely hidden in the screen
requirements.statement: A Staff member sending DELETE /api/products/{id} or PATCH /api/workspaces/{id}/settings directly is refused, and the product and settings are unchanged afterwards, while an Owner performing the same request succeeds
requirements.notes: Both halves are required: the refusal for the least-privileged role and the success for the owner, so over-refusal is detectable.

requirements.source_phrase: not being able to reach another company's data even by following a direct link or guessing an identifier
requirements.statement: A signed-in member of workspace B requesting GET /api/products/{id} or GET /api/products/{id}/movements with an id from workspace A is refused and receives no field of that product or its movements
requirements.notes: Direct-link and guessed-id boundary; the response must carry no partial payload.

requirements.source_phrase: Users can export the product list to CSV
requirements.statement: Clicking export on /products downloads a CSV named for the workspace and date whose rows are the products the screen is currently showing, including their quantities and stock values

requirements.source_phrase: Users can export the product list to CSV
requirements.statement: GET /api/products/export.csv returns a well-formed CSV whose header names the exported columns and whose rows and stock-value totals equal what the filtered list returns, scoped to the caller's workspace
requirements.notes: Judged by file content, not by response status: it must open as CSV and hold the same rows the screen shows.

requirements.statement: Creating a second product with a SKU already stored in the same workspace is refused by the store and stores no second row, including when two identical submissions arrive together
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of product creation: the unique SKU is a store constraint, not a form check, and the concurrent case is the one that exposes a read-then-write race.

requirements.statement: A stock movement that would take the on-hand quantity below zero is refused, no movement row is written, and the stored quantity is unchanged
requirements.notes: Boundary value of the stock calculation; also proves the failure path writes nothing half-way.

requirements.statement: A stock movement may be dated in the past and is accepted with that date; a movement dated in the future is refused and moves no quantity
requirements.notes: A ledger entry legitimately records something that already happened; a future-dated movement would corrupt the on-hand figure.

requirements.statement: The quantity and stock value a product row displays equal the values GET /api/products returns for that product after a reload, never a value left over from a previous row or from the browser only
GET /api/products, GET /api/dashboard and GET /api/products?low_stock=true for a brand-new workspace each return an empty result with zero totals rather than an error
After signing out from the header the app returns to /signin and makes no further signed-in request; pressing back does not render the previous workspace's product data
After sign-out the previous session token is refused by GET /api/products, and the token issued for a different session still works, so sign-out revokes one session only
A workspace with a thousand products renders its list by page and the first page appears in about the time a five-product list does, with the row count stated on screen
GET /api/products over a thousand stored rows returns each matching product exactly once across its pages, and the total count equals the number of rows the pages contain
A search term, category filter and sort order applied on /products survive a page reload and back-navigation, and clearing the filters resets the list to every product

Every stock value and total the API returns equals quantity times unit cost summed for its scope and rounded to the cent, so the product row, the dashboard total and the CSV export report the same figure for the same data
requirements.notes: Business logic class: one formula, one precision, applied on the list, the dashboard and the export path alike.

requirements.statement: The stock value shown on a product row, the inventory total on /dashboard and the figure in the exported CSV are identical for the same product and no value is rounded differently in one place than another

For any product, the currently stored quantity equals the starting quantity plus the sum of the deltas in its movement history, and deleting a movement is either refused or recomputes the quantity to match
requirements.notes: The ledger and the running total must not drift; this is the invariant that catches a double-applied movement.

requirements.statement: GET / serves the application shell and every asset it references, so /products, /dashboard and /settings each load with no 404 for a script or stylesheet and no unstyled flash
requirements.notes: Shared backend for the presentation-only frontend requirements (contrast, layout, routing, no-leak, build).

requirements.statement: Body text, table headers and the low-stock badge on /products meet at least a 4.5:1 contrast ratio against their background in the app's only theme, and the low-stock badge is distinguishable without relying on colour alone
requirements.notes: Layout, theme and visuals class; the palette is served through the shell's stylesheet.

requirements.statement: /products and /dashboard show their primary content without overlap or clipping at 1440px and at 375px wide, with the add-product action start-visible rather than behind a collapsed menu
Saving a product or a stock movement shows a confirmation naming the thing saved, and a refused save shows a message in the user's terms stating what was rejected; nothing succeeds or fails silently
A refused write returns a machine-readable error naming the field or rule that failed, and the client can render it without an unhandled exception or a bare stack trace
When a save, delete or stock movement fails the screen shows a message in the user's terms saying what went wrong, and the product list still shows the pre-action values
The header, page titles and empty-state copy name the product consistently and match the product the request describes, with no placeholder text or lorem ipsum on any screen
The URL reflects the current screen, so opening /products/{id} directly or reloading it lands on that product's detail with its data, and forward and back move between the screens already visited
requirements.notes: UI state, navigation and interaction class.

requirements.statement: On /products the loading, empty, populated and error states look visibly different from one another, and a control that renders performs its action exactly once and then shows its own new state
Opening /products or /dashboard while signed out redirects to /signin rather than rendering a blank page or another workspace's data
requirements.notes: Auth, sessions and access control class.

requirements.statement: Any /api route other than signup and signin refuses a request with no session or an expired session and returns no workspace data
A session token stays valid while the user works and refreshes before it expires, so a save made after twenty minutes of work still succeeds with no re-login

requirements.source_phrase: Two ways to sign in: Google, or email and password.
requirements.statement: The sign-in screen shows a Google button; completing the Google consent screen returns the visitor to the app signed in and the workspace lists that account's own projects
requirements.notes: Second entry path beside the email form; the return-to-app half is what a frontend test can see.

requirements.source_phrase: Two ways to sign in: Google, or email and password.
requirements.statement: GET /api/auth/google/callback checks the OAuth state value issued at sign-in start, exchanges the code for the provider-verified email and issues a session for that email; a callback whose state value does not match is refused and issues no session
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of Google sign-in: the state check and the verified email are what stop a forged callback. Third-party class as well as auth class.

requirements.source_phrase: If both use the same email address, they reach the same account.
requirements.statement: Signing in with Google as jane@studio.test and later registering with email/password as jane@studio.test reaches one account: projects created under either sign-in appear under both, and no second account row is stored for the same address
requirements.notes: Logical identity: the verified email address is the identity key; the sign-in method and any display name may change without creating a new account.

requirements.statement: admin@ue5architect.dev signs in with UE5Admin!2026 and is the single account flagged admin, so it can issue password-reset links and no other account can
requirements.notes: Seed value from required_credentials; the approved plan says 'A built-in admin account exists for the app owner.' Every reset-link test seeds from this account.

requirements.statement: tester@example.com signs in with Testpass123 and owns exactly one project named 'Legacy Health', which is shared with the admin as Viewer and has its public link switched on
requirements.notes: Seed from required_credentials and other_misc_info; the viewer-refusal and public-link tests read this project.

requirements.source_phrase: Reset works by a link shown on screen, because email sending is not part of this phase.
requirements.statement: From the account menu an admin can create a reset link for an account and the link is displayed on screen with a Copy control, while the Forgot password link explains that reset links are issued by the app owner rather than emailed
requirements.notes: The on-screen link is the whole delivery path in Phase 1; the build note says the link is created from the admin account menu, which is why the Forgot password copy must explain it.

requirements.source_phrase: Reset works by a link shown on screen, because email sending is not part of this phase.
requirements.statement: POST /api/auth/admin/reset-link as the admin returns a single-use token; POST /api/auth/reset/{token} sets the new password once and a second use of the same token is refused; the same create request from a non-admin returns 403 and issues no token
requirements.notes: Three behaviours in one promise: admin-only creation, single use, and the new password actually replacing the old one.

requirements.source_phrase: There are two lists, "Mine" and "Shared with me".
requirements.statement: The Projects screen shows a 'Mine' list and a 'Shared with me' list; a project the signed-in user owns appears only in Mine and a project shared with them appears only in Shared with me
requirements.notes: The library's two-way split; the mutual exclusion is the part worth testing.

requirements.source_phrase: There are two lists, "Mine" and "Shared with me".
requirements.statement: GET /api/projects returns the caller's owned projects under mine and the projects where the caller is Editor or Viewer under shared, with no project in both lists and no project the caller has no role on
requirements.notes: Scoping is by the caller's role, not by a client-supplied owner id.

requirements.source_phrase: the inputs that produced it: description, dials, Project Context, modules and notes
requirements.statement: Saving a synthesis creates or updates a project whose stored inputs are the description, dials, Project Context, module set and notes that produced the shown system; reopening the project from Projects restores those inputs and that system
requirements.notes: Reopening with the right prompt is what makes further tuning possible; a save that keeps only the output fails this.

requirements.source_phrase: the inputs that produced it: description, dials, Project Context, modules and notes
requirements.statement: POST /api/projects and PUT /api/projects/{id} write the system output and its inputs in one record; GET /api/projects/{id} from a new session returns the same description, dials, context, modules, notes and system body
requirements.notes: Proves the inputs object survives a new session, not just the browser cache.

requirements.source_phrase: The top bar gains the project name (editable in place)
requirements.statement: The project name in the top bar is editable in place and the new name survives a reload; deleting a project asks for confirmation naming it and the project disappears from both lists
requirements.notes: Rename in place is the named control; over-refusal of rename by an Editor would be a finding too.

requirements.source_phrase: Only the owner can delete a project, change roles or toggle the public link. Editors can regenerate, save and manage files. Viewers can read, copy and export.
requirements.statement: PATCH /api/projects/{id} stores a new name for an Owner or an Editor; DELETE /api/projects/{id} succeeds only for the Owner, removes the project and its files, and the project then returns 404 from its own URL and from /api/share/{token}
requirements.notes: Both halves: the Owner's delete succeeds and an Editor's is refused, so over-refusal is detectable.

requirements.source_phrase: Each project shows who last saved it and when.
requirements.statement: Each project in the Projects lists and the open project's header show which member last saved it and when, and the shown name and time change after another member saves the project
requirements.notes: The value must be the server record of the save, not a local timestamp.

requirements.source_phrase: Each project shows who last saved it and when.
requirements.statement: GET /api/projects/{id} returns last_saved_by naming the user who performed the last write and last_saved_at as the server timestamp of that write, and a save by a different member changes both fields
requirements.notes: Two savers are needed to prove the field tracks the writer rather than the owner.

requirements.source_phrase: If someone else saved while you were editing, you are warned before overwriting. You can then load their version or overwrite it.
requirements.statement: When another member has saved since the open project was loaded, pressing Save shows a dialog naming the other saver with 'Load their version' and 'Overwrite with mine'; Load replaces the editor with their saved system and Overwrite stores the local system
requirements.notes: Both branches of the dialog must be exercised; a dialog that offers only Overwrite fails the load path.

requirements.source_phrase: If someone else saved while you were editing, you are warned before overwriting. You can then load their version or overwrite it.
requirements.statement: PUT /api/projects/{id} with a base_version older than the stored version returns 409 carrying the current version and the last saver and writes nothing, while a PUT with the current base_version stores the change and increments the version by exactly one
requirements.notes: The refused PUT must leave the stored system byte-identical, which is the failure path the dialog cannot show.

requirements.source_phrase: Public share links are view-only and show the system and setup guide, but not project files.
requirements.statement: Opening /share/{token} with no session renders the project's pseudocode, .h, .cpp and setup guide, Copy JSON and Export JSON both work, and there is no Files tab or upload control on the page
requirements.notes: The signed-out exception to the sign-in requirement; the missing Files surface is part of the promise.

requirements.source_phrase: The owner can switch the link off at any time.
requirements.statement: GET /api/share/{token} serves the project read-only to a caller with no session and returns no file records; after the owner switches the link off the same GET returns 404 and the page renders a not-found state
requirements.notes: Switching off must actually revoke: a cached page that still renders after revocation is a finding.

requirements.source_phrase: Only the owner can delete a project, change roles or toggle the public link.
requirements.statement: Switching the project's public link on or off succeeds for the Owner and is refused for an Editor or a Viewer, with the link state unchanged after the refused request
requirements.notes: Privacy boundary reached by a direct request; the Owner half proves the endpoint is not simply always off.

requirements.source_phrase: Only the owner can delete a project, change roles or toggle the public link. Editors can regenerate, save and manage files. Viewers can read, copy and export.
requirements.statement: For a project shared as Viewer, POST /api/projects/{id}/files, PUT /api/projects/{id} and a generate request attributed to that project are refused and write nothing, while the same three requests from an Editor of the project succeed
requirements.notes: Server-side enforcement of the Editor/Viewer split, checked with direct requests rather than through the disabled controls.

requirements.source_phrase: Viewers see the same workspace, with editing controls disabled and a clear "View only" badge.
requirements.statement: A Viewer opening the project sees a 'View only' badge, the Synthesize, Save, slider, module and upload controls disabled and no Share button, while Copy JSON, Export JSON and file downloads still work
requirements.notes: The read-only paths must stay enabled; hiding them as well would be over-refusal.

requirements.source_phrase: The owner can also copy an invite link to send themselves.
requirements.statement: The Owner adds an address as Editor or Viewer in the Share modal and gets a copyable invite link; the invitee signed in as that address and opening /invite/{token} joins the project with that role and finds it under Shared with me
requirements.notes: The link is the delivery path while no real emails are sent in Phase 1.

requirements.source_phrase: An invite is sent to an email address.
requirements.statement: POST /api/projects/{id}/invites records the invite bound to that project and role; POST /api/invites/{token}/accept adds the signed-in caller to that project only and only once, is refused when the caller's email differs from the invited address, and grants no access to any other project
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of the invite: single use, bound to the address, bound to the project.

requirements.source_phrase: The person sees the project under "Shared with me" as soon as they sign in with that email.
requirements.statement: A member who signs in with the address a pending invite names finds that project under Shared with me without opening any link, whether they sign in with Google or with email and password
requirements.notes: The wider rule the user's line sets; the build narrows auto-apply to Google-verified addresses, so the email/password path is the one Phase 4 should report.

requirements.source_phrase: A paperclip on the description box lets you attach up to 5 files to the next synthesis.
requirements.statement: The description box has a paperclip that attaches up to 5 reference files; each attached reference is listed under the description with its own remove control and stays attached to the project for later regenerations
requirements.notes: The paperclip is the control; the listed-and-removable state is what proves the attachment stuck.

requirements.source_phrase: Accepted types are screenshots and images, PDFs, and code or text files (.h, .cpp, .txt, .md, .json).
requirements.statement: POST /api/projects/{id}/references stores an attached image, PDF, .h, .cpp, .txt, .md or .json file up to 10 MB under its original name and refuses a sixth attachment, an oversized file or a disallowed type such as .exe with a message naming the rule and no stored row
requirements.notes: Type list, 10 MB ceiling and the five-file cap all trace to the same [USER] plan; the refused upload must leave nothing stored.

requirements.source_phrase: A "Files" tab on each project, for anything the team wants to keep with the system
requirements.statement: A project's Files tab lists its files with name, size and uploader; uploading a file adds it to the list, downloading returns a file with the original name and identical bytes, and deleting removes the row from the list
requirements.notes: Download equality is judged by the file's content, not by the response status.

requirements.source_phrase: File limits: 10 MB per reference file and 25 MB per project file.
requirements.statement: POST /api/projects/{id}/files stores a file up to 25 MB and refuses a larger one with a message naming the limit; GET of a stored file returns the same bytes under its original name; DELETE removes it and a later GET returns 404
requirements.notes: Project files have a different ceiling from reference files; a viewer's upload or delete goes through roles-enforced-be.

requirements.source_phrase: **Export JSON** downloads the project. A new **Copy JSON** button copies it to the clipboard.
requirements.statement: Export JSON on an open project downloads a .json named for the project and Copy JSON puts the same document on the clipboard; importing that document through Import project creates a new project with the same description, inputs and system output
requirements.notes: Two controls, one document; the round trip is the assertion.

requirements.source_phrase: **Import project** loads an exported .json file back in as a new project.
requirements.statement: GET /api/projects/{id}/export returns a JSON document holding the project's system output and inputs; POST /api/projects/import with that document creates a new project owned by the caller whose inputs and system output equal the exported ones
requirements.notes: The importer must not inherit the source project's members or public link.

requirements.source_phrase: **First sign-in:** if systems are saved in this browser, a prompt offers two choices.
requirements.statement: On first sign-in with systems saved in this browser a modal offers 'Import them' and 'Start fresh'; Import creates one project per browser system in the account, Start fresh leaves them in the browser, and the modal does not appear again after either choice
requirements.notes: Both choices must be exercised; a prompt that reappears after Start fresh is the failure the plan names.

requirements.source_phrase: **First sign-in:** if systems are saved in this browser, a prompt offers two choices.
requirements.statement: POST /api/projects/import-legacy creates one project per system in the posted browser library for the caller and creates no duplicate project when the same payload is posted twice
requirements.notes: Idempotence is the paranoid half: a retried import must not double the library.

requirements.source_phrase: When the user changes parameters, toggles modules, or adds notes before hitting Synthesize, those changes must be clearly injected into the next generation context.
requirements.statement: Every change made since the last synthesis — description, dials, class, NET, parameter values, module toggles and additions, and notes — appears in a 'Queued for next synthesis' list, the button reads 'Regenerate with N changes' with N equal to the listed items, and after the run an 'Applied in this synthesis' panel lists each change with its outcome
requirements.notes: The count on the button and the row per change in the applied panel are what make 'visibly respect the edits' testable.

requirements.source_phrase: When the user changes parameters, toggles modules, or adds notes before hitting Synthesize, those changes must be clearly injected into the next generation context.
requirements.statement: POST /api/generate receives the queued changes and the previous system, sends each change as an explicit instruction alongside the previous output, and the stored synthesis records one applied entry per queued change so the applied panel has a row for each
requirements.notes: A regenerate that silently starts from scratch instead of revising the previous system fails this.

requirements.source_phrase: These should appear in the Blueprint Pseudocode and Setup Guide tabs.
requirements.statement: The Blueprint Pseudocode tab shows inline yellow 'Why' callouts on key decisions with a control to show or hide them, and each Setup Guide step shows its own Why note beneath it
requirements.notes: Both tabs and the show/hide control; a note only in one tab fails the promise.

requirements.source_phrase: Add short inline callouts to the generated output explaining *why* key decisions were made.
requirements.statement: The stored synthesis carries one why-note per annotated pseudocode block and one per setup step, each naming the decision it explains (replication, Data Asset choice or similar) rather than restating the step
requirements.notes: Judged on the note's content against a known system, not on the field being present.

requirements.source_phrase: Add a single optional text field (e.g. "Project Context")
requirements.statement: An optional 'Project Context' field under the description accepts a short preset, is remembered in the browser across reloads, and is sent with every synthesis without appearing in the description field
requirements.notes: Silent prepending is the point: the description box must stay clean while the context still steers output.

requirements.source_phrase: This gets prepended to every synthesis silently
requirements.statement: Every POST /api/generate places the stored Project Context before the description in the model prompt, and the saved project's inputs record the context value that was used
requirements.notes: Checked by comparing output for the same description with and without a context preset.

requirements.source_phrase: The user should be able to select two or more saved systems and combine them into a single synthesized output that references shared attributes and avoids conflicts.
requirements.statement: Ticking 2–4 systems in the library enables 'Stack N systems'; the result header names the combined systems, shared attributes appear as chips each with a single owning module, and every conflict the merge resolved is listed
requirements.notes: The chips and the conflict list are the visible evidence that shared attributes were merged rather than duplicated.

requirements.source_phrase: The user should be able to select two or more saved systems and combine them into a single synthesized output that references shared attributes and avoids conflicts.
requirements.statement: POST /api/stack with fewer than 2 or more than 4 system ids is refused and starts no generation; with 2–4 ids it returns one merged system whose parameter list holds each shared attribute once and a conflicts list naming each resolved conflict
requirements.notes: Boundary values 1 and 5 are the paranoid half of the 2–4 selection.

requirements.source_phrase: Show the previous and current synthesis side by side so the user can see the effect of dial or prompt changes.
requirements.statement: The Compare tab shows the previous and current synthesis side by side with removed lines in red and added lines in green, switches between pseudocode, .h, .cpp, setup guide and parameters and modules, opens automatically after every regeneration, and lists which inputs changed
requirements.notes: Five sections, auto-open and the changed-inputs list are each separate assertions.

requirements.source_phrase: Show the previous and current synthesis side by side so the user can see the effect of dial or prompt changes.
requirements.statement: GET /api/projects/{id}/versions/compare returns the previous and current text of each of the five sections plus the list of changed inputs; a project with a single synthesis returns an empty previous side rather than an error
requirements.notes: The first-synthesis case is the empty state Compare must survive.

requirements.source_phrase: Do not add a "this is a sketch" disclaimer for now.
requirements.statement: No 'this is a sketch' or placeholder disclaimer appears on any tab of a generated system, in the exported JSON or on the public share view
requirements.notes: A promise of absence; it is testable by searching the rendered output and the exported document.

requirements.statement: POST /api/generate returns a system whose event graph has nodes and edges, whose pseudocode carries why-notes, whose .h and .cpp files are non-empty and syntactically complete, and whose setup guide has numbered steps, with no field holding a sketch or placeholder disclaimer
requirements.notes: Build description: the backend returns a schema-validated SystemOutput (nodes/edges/modules/params/cpp/pseudocode/setup). Judged on the content of each part.

requirements.statement: A synthesis for the description 'inventory system with stacking' returns nodes and setup steps naming inventory concepts such as add item, stack count and max stack, while a synthesis of 'melee combat combo' returns different nodes naming combat concepts, so no fixed reply is reused across inputs
requirements.notes: AI class: the output must be right for its input on a case whose answer is known in advance, and must change when the input changes.

requirements.statement: Pressing Synthesize shows a running state with a progress counter and a disabled button while the job runs, then replaces it with the finished system; a job that fails shows an error where the result would be instead of an empty tab
requirements.notes: Build description: generation runs in the background, the page polls, a progress counter is shown; runs take roughly 40–90 seconds.

requirements.statement: POST /api/generate starts a background job and returns its id; GET /api/generate/{job_id} reports running with a progress value until it returns the complete SystemOutput, and reports a failed status with a reason when the provider call fails, storing no partial system
requirements.notes: Build description: generation runs in the background on the server while the page checks back every 2 seconds; a long job must not be reported as an empty result.

requirements.statement: POST /api/generate without a session returns 401 and starts no job, and GET /api/generate/{job_id} returns 404 to any caller other than the job's creator with no partial output
requirements.notes: Build description: generation now requires auth and a job is visible only to its creator; the job id is the guessed identifier that must not leak another user's output.

requirements.statement: Setting the Max Health slider to 250 and pressing Synthesize produces .h and .cpp text containing 250 for that parameter, and the same value is stored on the slider and in the project's saved inputs
requirements.notes: Build description: values set on the parameter sliders are written into the code on the next synthesis. One value, three places, all equal.

requirements.statement: Turning a module chip off and regenerating returns a system with that module's params, nodes and code absent, and turning it back on returns them, with the module list in the stored inputs matching the chips
requirements.notes: Build description: turning a module off now really removes it instead of being asked for and removed at once.

requirements.source_phrase: The AI uses them as source material, e.g. "extend this existing header" or "match this UI screenshot".
requirements.statement: A synthesis with an attached .h reference file returns a .h that extends that file's declared class, and a synthesis with a UI screenshot attached returns setup steps that follow the widgets mounted in the screenshot rather than an unrelated layout
requirements.notes: The reference must reach the model prompt; an attachment that is stored but ignored fails this on content.

requirements.statement: When a generation fails because the Universal Key balance is exhausted or the provider errors out, the workspace shows a friendly message naming the cause, the running state ends, and no placeholder system is rendered
requirements.notes: Build description: a budget-exceeded error is shown as a friendly message. A spinner that never resolves or a canned system both fail.

requirements.statement: A provider timeout, rate-limit or insufficient-balance response marks the job failed with a machine-readable reason and the provider's own message, stores no system, and a retry of the same request stores exactly one system
requirements.notes: Third-party class: the failure is reported in the user's terms and the retry does not duplicate the side effect.

requirements.statement: The description box shows a live character counter against a 2,000-character limit, refuses to submit beyond it, and the message names the limit
requirements.notes: Build description: the description box has a 2,000-character limit with a counter.

requirements.statement: POST /api/generate refuses a description longer than 2,000 characters with a message naming the limit and starts no job
requirements.notes: The client counter is not the enforcement; the boundary is 2,000 accepted and 2,001 refused.

requirements.statement: The Event Graph renders the generated nodes and bezier wires, pans and zooms with the mouse wheel, drags a node to a new position, responds to touch, and the Fit button frames every node in view
requirements.notes: Build description: draggable nodes with bezier wires, touch support, mouse-wheel zoom and a Fit button; node positions come from the stored graph.

requirements.statement: The workspace offers template system cards (inventory, combat, dialogue, AI and similar) and choosing one fills the description with that template's prompt so Synthesis can run from it
requirements.notes: benchmark: describe-to-system tools open with starter templates so the first synthesis does not need a blank-page prompt.

requirements.statement: GET /api/templates returns the eight template cards with a title and a description that POST /api/generate accepts, and each template's description synthesizes into a system naming that template's subject
requirements.notes: benchmark: the template gallery is only real if a card's prompt actually generates that kind of system.

requirements.statement: A new account with no projects shows an explicit empty message in both Mine and Shared with me, and a project with no files shows an empty Files tab with an upload action rather than a blank panel
requirements.notes: Tier-1 empty state; a brand-new account and a freshly created project are both met before any data exists.

requirements.statement: Opening /projects/{id} directly in a fresh tab while signed in loads that project's saved system, its inputs and its Files tab, and a reload keeps the same project open
requirements.notes: UI state and navigation: the URL reflects the open project and survives a reload, including from a deep link.

requirements.statement: After the Owner changes a member's role from Editor to Viewer, that member's next PUT /api/projects/{id} is refused with no write and their next GET returns the project in read-only form, within one request of the change
requirements.notes: A role change must take effect on the next request rather than at the next sign-in.

requirements.source_phrase: The current dark Unreal Editor look stays: slate panels, Unreal orange accents and monospace details.
requirements.statement: The sign-in screen, workspace, Share modal and public share view all use the dark Unreal Editor palette of slate panels with orange accents and monospace details, the sign-in screen carries a blueprint-grid background, the app mark, the Google button and the email form, and body text meets at least a 4.5:1 contrast against its background
requirements.notes: Layout, theme and UX class: one palette across four surfaces, with the contrast ratio named so it can be measured.

requirements.statement: GET /assets/index.css serves the single stylesheet every screen imports and it defines the slate background and orange accent tokens consumed by the workspace, the sign-in screen and the public share view, with no per-screen inline colour override
requirements.notes: The same component must render the same way on every page; one token source is the mechanism the screens depend on.

requirements.statement: /login, /workspace and /share/{token} show their primary content and their Synthesize or Copy JSON action without overlap or clipping at 1440px and at 375px wide
requirements.notes: Tier-2 layout class; the build note says the layout is desktop only, so this requirement records the gap for Phase 4 to report.

requirements.statement: The workspace polls a running generation job on a single timer, stops polling when the job finishes or the user leaves the workspace, and returning to the workspace shows one live poll rather than several
requirements.notes: Performance and resource leaks: opening and leaving the workspace repeatedly must not stack timers.

requirements.statement: The Emergent Universal Key and the Google OAuth client secret are read from the server environment, never appear in a page, an API response, a log line or the client bundle, and the server starts with no unset required setting
requirements.notes: Third-party and build classes: the browser calls only this app's own endpoints, so no provider key can reach it.
